chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Bukayr, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

A man asked him about two sisters and a husband, so he said: 'The half and the half'. So the man said, 'May Allah keep you well! Allah has named for them both more than this. For the two of them is the two-thirds'. So he said: 'So what would you say regarding a brother and a husband?' So he said, 'The half and the half'. So he said, 'Has not Allah named the wealth, so He said [4:176] and he shall be her heir when there is no child for her?'
ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of a brother and a husband when there are no children?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Imam’s pedagogical method of using a general ruling to test the questioner’s familiarity with Quranic inheritance laws before addressing specific scenarios. It clarifies the distribution between a brother and a husband when there are no descendants, highlighting the interplay between the Quranic text and the Imam’s authoritative interpretation. This dialogue underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Imam’s role in elucidating the precise application of divine law in complex familial inheritance cases.
